Subject: AcmeCorp demo recap + next steps (security ask)

Hi Alice / Acme team,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on the discovery call: 

- Scope: PII from end-user inputs (chat + file attachments) is retained for up to 30 days for debugging by default; export/retention options available for enterprise contracts.
- Deployment option discussed: Dedicated capacity (VPC) to meet compliance boundary requirements.
- Performance SLOs: target 150ms p50 for typical chat workloads.

Security/compliance next steps I promised:
1) Share our current subprocessor list + short SOC 2 summary (attached).
2) Start the vendor security questionnaire — we can either fill your XLS or share our standard questionnaire.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with our security lead to walk through any detailed questions.

I've attached a PDF with the current subprocessor inventory and a one-page SOC 2 summary. If you prefer, we can drop a spreadsheet version of the SOC evidence into your portal/Drive.

Would you prefer we: (A) fill out your vendor questionnaire and return it to security@acmecorp.com, or (B) share our questionnaire and evidence bundle in a Drive folder?

Next availability for a short call: Wed 3/10 10-12 PT or Thu 3/11 9-11 PT.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the attachments. A few quick asks from our InfoSec team before we loop in procurement: 

- Can you confirm Redwood's current SOC 2 status (Type II, date of most recent audit) and provide the auditor contact if available?
- We need an explicit list of subprocessors (cloud infra + third-party model providers, analytics vendors, monitoring). The PDF looks good but can you also provide a machine-readable spreadsheet?
- Acme handles regulated PHI in some product lines — please confirm whether Redwood supports HIPAA and what controls you put in place for PHI in transit and at rest.

We'd prefer (A) you fill our vendor security questionnaire (attached) and return, and (B) grant a Drive folder with evidence. I'll forward the questionnaire to the security alias.

Can we target Thu 3/11 10am PT for the security call?

Alice

Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeCorp demo recap + next steps (security ask)

Hi Alice —

Thanks — we can do that. Quick answers up front:
- SOC 2: We completed a SOC 2 Type II in Nov 2026. I'll attach the SOC 2 summary (redwood_soc2_summary_2026.pdf) and can provide a redacted full report under NDA. Auditor: PineTree LLP (audit@pinetree-llp.com).
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA-covered workloads via Private deployment (customer-managed VPC + KMS). We maintain encryption at rest (AES-256) and TLS 1.2+ in transit; we also provide configuration guidance for minimizing PHI exposure (no long-term retention, strict RBAC).
- Subprocessors: Attached PDF is the canonical list; I'll also attach a spreadsheet version and start filling your XLS. High-level subprocessors: AWS (S3/EC2), GCP (BigQuery for analytics in some deployments), Cloudflare (CDN), Segment/Amplitude (opt-in telemetry), Sentry (error reporting), and a few niche vendors for monitoring. Third-party model providers we use for model cataloging/benching: OpenModelHub (contracted) - not a data processor for customer prompt data by default unless explicitly configured.

Action plan:
- I will: (1) upload a spreadsheet version of the subprocessor list to the Drive folder, (2) begin answering the vendor_security_questionnaire_acme.xlsx and return a first pass by EOD Wed 3/10, (3) drop the SOC 2 summary into the Drive folder and open access for the Acme security alias.
- Rishi: can you double-check the PHI guidance and add a short blurb we can share with the customer about our Private deployment controls?
- Stephanie: can you own the questionnaire fill and return?

Confirming Thu 3/11 10am PT works for the call. We'll send a calendar invite once we have the Drive folder link.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Stephanie -

Thanks for taking point. A couple of internal notes / suggested language for the customer re: PHI and subprocessors: 

- PHI boundary: "Redwood does not index or use customer prompt data for model training unless customers opt in. For Private deployments, all compute and storage are provisioned within the customer's VPC and keys are customer-managed."
- Subprocessor nuance: Call out "OpenModelHub is used for model cataloging and research-only telemetry; it does not receive customer prompt or output data unless a customer explicitly selects an external model that requires forwarding."
- For AWS/GCP: provide region-level data residency notes (e.g., US-EAST-1, europe-west1) and confirm that we can restrict storage to customer-specified regions under Dedicated/Private contracts.

Recommendation: include a short annex in the Drive folder that maps each subprocessor to the specific function (storage, telemetry, analytics) and data categories handled (metadata only vs. content). That tends to speed review.

I can draft the annex and the PHI blurb - will put drafts in the Drive folder by EOD.

- Rishi
